identity.title: Unveiling the gas phase H<SUB>2</SUB>NCO radical: Laboratory rotational spectroscopy and interstellar searches in the direction of IRAS 16293-2422

paper_type_evidence.quote: To test the new spectroscopic predictions for , we carried out a search for it using the data from the Protostellar Interferometric Line Survey (PILS).

question.value: Can the gas-phase rotational spectrum of the H2NCO radical be measured in the laboratory and used to search for the radical toward IRAS 16293-2422 in PILS data?

evidence.quote: In order to enable interstellar searches of , we have undertaken a mandatory laboratory characterisation of its pure rotational spectrum.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00278.S.
in band 7
This survey, which covers the spectral range 329–363 GHz
(both spin-rotation components around 342.957 and 343.059 GHz)
(around 343.109 GHz)
with the Atacama Large millimetre/submillimetre Array (ALMA) 12 m array and the Atacama Compact Array (ACA) in band 7
It has a spatial resolution of $\sim$0.5$\ensuremath{''}$
a sensitivity of 4–5 mJy beam$^{-1}$ for a bin width of 1 km s$^{-1}$

what.value: NH2CHO and HNCO column densities (1.0e16 and 2.7e16 cm-2) toward IRAS16293 B

evidence.quote: found column densities of NH$_2$CHO and HNCO equal to 1.0 $\times$ 10$^{16}$ and 2.7 $\times$ 10$^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$, respectively
a $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 68 (cite: Milam2005)

evidence.quote: which uses the Nautilus code (cite: RN7545)—a 3-phase gas, dust grain ice surface, and dust grain ice mantle time dependent chemical model

what.value: PILS data, spectrum extraction position and LTE search follow earlier molecular studies

evidence.quote: compared to the spectrum extracted at the same position as the previous molecular studies

what.value: Chemical model as used in earlier work, initial abundances and collapse phase from Manigand2021

evidence.quote: the same initial abundances than in (cite: Manigand2021)

analysis_steps.goal: LTE spectral search and upper limits

method.value: LTE models from CASSIS compared to the PILS spectrum; brightest uncontaminated lines used for column density upper limits

evidence.quote: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) models were produced with the CASSIS software

key_parameters.value: linewidth 1 km/s, source size 0.5 arcsec, vLSR 2.7 km/s, Tex 125 and 300 K

evidence.quote: The models assume a linewidth of 1 km s$^{-1}$, a source size of 0.5$\ensuremath{''}$ and a $\varv_{\rm LSR}$ of 2.7 km s$^{-1}$
The excitation temperatures of complex organic molecules vary in this source between $\sim$125 K and 300 K

analysis_steps.goal: Compare abundance limit with chemical model

method.value: Compare upper limit with Nautilus model abundances

evidence.quote: we compare the upper limit derived above to the calculated abundance obtained using the model

key_parameters.value: density 2.5e4 cm-3, 10 K, Av 10 mag, zeta 1.3e-17 s-1

evidence.quote: homogeneous gas with a density equal to $2.5\times10^4$ cm$^{-3}$; temperature of 10 K for both gas and dust
Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) models were produced with the CASSIS[^1] software
which uses the Nautilus code (cite: RN7545)

used_for.value: line search and assignment in lab spectra

evidence.quote: We used the PGOPHER program (cite: western2017:PGOPHER) to search for, and assign, transitions
The final fit and spectral predictions were performed with the Pickett CALPGM suite of programs
All calculations were performed using the GAUSSIAN 16 suite of electronic structure programs

results_numeric.quantity: H2NCO column density upper limit, Tex~300 K

evidence.quote: the upper limit is estimated to be about 1.7 $\times$ 10$^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$

results_numeric.quantity: H2NCO column density upper limit, Tex~125 K

evidence.quote: found a very close upper limit of 8.0 $\times$ 10$^{13}$ cm$^{-2}$
an upper limit of 7 $\times$ 10$^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$ for $T_{\rm ex}$ = 300 K and 5 $\times$ 10$^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$ for $T_{\rm ex}$ = 125 K
The fit takes a root-mean-square value of 107 kHz and a reduced standard deviation of 0.84.

findings_qualitative.value: H2NCO is not detected; abundance is at least 60 times below formamide and 160 times below HNCO, consistent with the chemical model

evidence.quote: The inferred upper limit shows that abundance is at least 60 times below that of formamide and 160 times below that of HNCO in this source

claims.hypothesis: Is H2NCO detectable in PILS toward IRAS16293 B with the new catalogue?
claims.experiment: LTE search with CASSIS at Tex 125-300 K
claims.result: No lines above noise; N upper limits 8e13-1.7e14 cm-2
claims.finding: Not detected; at least 60x less abundant than formamide

evidence.quote: No transitions of the radical were detected on the PILS survey.

claims.hypothesis: Is the non-detection consistent with a physico-chemical model?
claims.result: Radicals are destroyed on grains before desorption

evidence.quote: a value that is in agreement with predictions from a physico-chemical model of this young protostar

why_this_data.value: IRAS16293 B is a source where formamide and related molecules were already detected

evidence.quote: A search for the H$_2$NCO radical is consequently pertinent towards this source.

referee_caveats_inferred: Upper limits rely on LTE and an assumed 0.5 arcsec source size
Limits are derived without stated noise or uncertainty
Lab catalogue accuracy is only 100 kHz
